conventions.convention: S is finite; W need not be finite. Empty generating subsets give the trivial parabolic subgroup.
D_L(w) tests left multiplication and D_R(w) tests right multiplication. W^I has no right descents in I and represents left cosets wW_I; ^IW has no left descents in I and represents right cosets W_Iw.
For d ∈ ^IW^J, K={s ∈ I : d⁻¹sd ∈ J}; the normal form restricts its first factor to W_I^K, the elements of W_I without right descents in K.
Bruhat edges are u→ut for reflections t with strictly increasing length. Bruhat order permits the empty chain; inversion preserves the order, and distinct equal-length elements are incomparable.
Subword positions are indexed from 1; the empty subword is allowed. A subword witness may be reduced by two-letter deletions to one of length ℓ(u).

Deletion labels are original positions in one fixed reduced expression of the top, read along descending saturated chains. Labels depend on the root chain above an edge; comparisons between different fixed expressions are not asserted.
Shelling uses the earlier-facet codimension-one intersection criterion. The order complex of an empty open interval is {∅}, with one empty facet.
The Eulerian sign formula concerns full Bruhat intervals. It is not asserted for induced parabolic quotient intervals; rank-zero chains have empty, vacuously falling label words.
The S4 examples display letters 1,2,3,4 by order-preserving transport from the library's zero-based permutation notation. Products act with the right factor first, and length is inversion number.

load_bearing.statement: For every fixed reduced expression w=s₁⋯s_q and every u ∈ W, u≤w iff u is the product of a subword; the indices may be chosen with k=ℓ(u). Equivalently, a reduced subword expression of u occurs in every reduced expression of w iff it occurs in some reduced expression. The empty subword gives 1≤w.

If u=s₁⋯s_q is reduced and ℓ(ut)<ℓ(u) for t ∈ T, exactly one position is deleted, with t the corresponding suffix-conjugated simple reflection. For a reduced subword expression of u≠w in a fixed reduced expression w, choose deleted positions i₁<⋯<i_k with i_k minimal. Restoring position i_k gives a reduced expression of ut of length ℓ(u)+1 and a Bruhat edge u→ut.

For u≤v, [u,v] is finite, with an injection into {0,1}^ℓ(v). Every strict comparison admits a Bruhat chain increasing length by one at each step. Every maximal chain in [u,v] has ℓ(v)−ℓ(u) strict steps, and x↦ℓ(x)−ℓ(u) is its rank function.

For u≤v and s ∈ S: opposite ascent/descent gives us≤v and u≤vs; common ascents give us≤vs and u≤vs; common descents give us≤vs and us≤v; a descent of u and ascent of v give us≤v and u≤vs. Covers are exactly comparable pairs of length difference one, equivalently u=vt with t ∈ T and ℓ(vt)=ℓ(v)−1. Single-letter deletions of a fixed reduced expression lie strictly below its value and are covers exactly when reduced; every cover has a unique deleted position. Bruhat order is directed.

For all I,J⊆S, W_I∩W_J=W_(I∩J). For every I, ρ(W_I) preserves V_I and Φ_I=Φ∩V_I, with the inherited sign decomposition; reflections in W_I correspond exactly to Φ_I⁺. Each left coset wW_I has one element d ∈ W^I of minimum length, and equality ℓ(x)=ℓ(d) within that coset forces x=d; the mirrored statement holds for right cosets and ^IW.

With a fixed total order on finite S, the specified left-first descent reduction terminates within ℓ(d) replacements at an element of W_IdW_J∩^IW^J. Every d ∈ ^IW^J is the unique minimum-length element of its double coset. Every x ∈ W_IdW_J admits x=udv with u ∈ W_I, v ∈ W_J and ℓ(x)=ℓ(u)+ℓ(d)+ℓ(v).

For d ∈ ^IW^J and K={s ∈ I : d⁻¹sd ∈ J}, W_I∩dW_Jd⁻¹=W_K and d⁻¹W_Kd=W_(d⁻¹Kd). Every letter s_i of a reduced I-expression of an element of that intersection satisfies d⁻¹s_id ∈ J. For s ∈ I, the conjugated positive root is simple in Φ_J iff d⁻¹sd ∈ J; if d⁻¹sd ∈ W_J then already d⁻¹sd ∈ J.

Every double coset has exactly one representative d ∈ ^IW^J, its unique minimum. For K={s ∈ I : d⁻¹sd ∈ J}, multiplication (u,v)↦udv is a bijection W_I^K×W_J→W_IdW_J and ℓ(udv)=ℓ(u)+ℓ(d)+ℓ(v). Consequently |W_IdW_J|=|W_I^K|·|W_J|; if W_I is finite this is (|W_I|/|W_K|)·|W_J|, with cardinal multiplication. Allowing arbitrary first factors in W_I destroys uniqueness in general.

Every rooted interval has at most one increasing maximal chain. A rank-two interval is a four-element diamond with label words (i,j) and (p,m), where i<j≤p and m<p. Every rooted interval has exactly one increasing maximal chain, lexicographically first. Replacing a falling two-step segment by the increasing chain of its rooted rank-two interval gives a lexicographically earlier chain differing at exactly the middle vertex.

The deleted-position labeling satisfies (N) and (L) on every rooted interval. If λ(m′)≺λ(m), there is k with λ(k)≺λ(m), m′∩m⊆k∩m and |k∩m|=|m|−1. Thus lexicographically ordered maximal chains of (u,v) shell its order complex. For rank zero or one the sole facet is empty; for rank two the open interval has two incomparable elements and either facet order shells it.

P^I is order-preserving, P^I(w)≤w, and equality holds exactly for w ∈ W^I. A cover y of x ∈ W^I either lies in W^I or equals xs for s ∈ I. The induced quotient order retains the subword criterion, finite intervals and chains increasing ambient length by one; maximal chains have the ambient length difference. W^I is directed and, if finite, has a unique maximum.

For full Bruhat intervals, Σ_(x∈[u,v]) (−1)^ℓ(x)=δ_(u,v)(−1)^ℓ(u), μ(u,v)=(−1)^(ℓ(v)−ℓ(u)), and the fixed-expression deleted-position labeling has exactly one strictly falling maximal chain. The sign formula is not asserted for proper parabolic quotient intervals.

published_dependencies.used_for: Finite-rank presentation, universal property, reduced words, length and empty-word conventions.
Simple length changes, sign parity, exchange and value-preserving two-letter deletion.
Support, intrinsic parabolic systems, both coset factorizations, inversion of length and the type-A identification.
Exact infinite-dihedral orders and ambient reducedness of alternating words.
Canonical real form and reflection formula, without nondegeneracy or definiteness assumptions.
Canonical homomorphism, root system, positive cone and conjugate reflection set.
Form preservation, unit root norms and conjugation of root reflections.
Signed root decomposition and coefficient-sign arguments in the parabolic root-subsystem proof.
Root-sign tests for length and positivity of conjugated roots.
Root-reflection dictionary and unique strong-exchange deletion; supplies the right-handed exchange lemma by inversion.
Descending rooted-chain labels, increasing and falling words, lexicographic order and exact (N)/(L) hypotheses.
Earlier/later facet comparison, endpoint removal and the falling-chain Möbius formula for finite graded rooted intervals satisfying (N)/(L).
Associativity, inverses, cancellation and conjugation identities.
Homomorphisms to Z/2 distinguishing dihedral conjugacy classes and subgroup cosets.
Standard parabolic and reflection subgroup constructions, including the empty generating set.
Left cosets gH and right cosets Hg; fixes terminology against multiplication-side ambiguity.
Nonnegative lengths, zero-length cases and finite induction parameters.
Attained minimum lengths in nonempty cosets and double cosets.
Parabolic simple-root spans and finite coordinate combinations.
Coordinates of V_I vanish outside I; V_∅={0}.
Zero-based permutation notation and composition with the right factor first.
Lengths and descent computations in the S4 examples.
Finite interval counts and parity-balance counts.
Cover and rank conventions on finite intervals.
Closed intervals and local finiteness.
Faces, vertices and the empty simplex convention.
Order-complex faces as finite chains and the vertex-free complex {∅}.
Integer-valued Möbius function on locally finite posets.
Diagonal values, both off-diagonal recurrences and uniqueness; used for the Eulerian theorem and quotient counterexample.

seams_checked.note: Owned Definition (1)–(2) and theorem F1 preserve support, intrinsic length, coset orientation, uniqueness and additivity. The double-coset reduction uses the stated two-letter deletion property.
The root-subsystem theorem F5–F7 and intersection lemma F4–F6 retain the signed canonical real roots, right root-length criterion, dictionary and strong-exchange hypotheses; no definiteness is added.
The right-exchange lemma F1 quotes the left strong-exchange statement accurately and derives its right-handed form by reversing reduced expressions and inverting the equality.

The shelling theorem F7–F8 and Eulerian theorem F9 preserve finite grading, descending rooted labels, (N)/(L), endpoint removal and the falling-chain count. They do not substitute ordinary edge labels for rooted labels.

The spherical definition uses W_T=⟨T⟩. The coset-intersection lemma F3 states W_I∩W_J=W_(I∩J) for all subsets and applies it after choosing a common coset point. The face-metric lemma F3 uses precisely invariance of V_U.

The series definition preserves D_L/D_R. The orbit-distance lemma F2 and Proof 3.1/6.1 preserve left-coset minima and right-factor additivity, including infinite W_T. The growth theorem retains both additive parabolic factorizations.

This is a declared contextual prerequisite. The current four interface items contain no citation or mathematical restatement of an owned parabolic or double-coset result; no altered supplier proposition was found.

The weak-order Definition and cited Facts preserve the left/right descent conventions. The full-descent lemma Statement (2) and F9 retain V_J invariance, Φ_J=Φ∩V_J and its inherited signs for the intrinsic parabolic system.
